title: Salesforce Developer
description: A comprehensive roadmap for aspiring Salesforce Developers, covering core CRM fundamentals, declarative and programmatic development with Apex and Lightning Web Components, integrations, DevOps practices, and preparing for industry-standard certifications and real-world projects.

tree.name: Salesforce Platform Fundamentals
tree.description: Develop a solid understanding of CRM concepts, the Salesforce ecosystem, declarative customization, data architecture, and robust security models.

children.name: CRM Concepts & Salesforce Ecosystem Overview
children.description: Grasp core CRM principles, understand the Salesforce Customer 360 vision, explore various Salesforce Clouds (Sales Cloud, Service Cloud, Experience Cloud, Marketing Cloud, Analytics Cloud, etc.), AppExchange, and the multi-tenant architecture to comprehend the platform's breadth and capabilities.

children.name: Declarative Customization & Automation (Admin Essentials)
children.description: Master standard and custom objects, fields, relationships, page layouts, record types, compact layouts, path, profiles, permission sets, roles, sharing settings, validation rules, formula fields, rollup summary fields, and powerful automation tools like Salesforce Flow (Screen Flow, Record-Triggered Flow, Schedule-Triggered Flow, Autolaunched Flow) to build robust business logic without code.

children.name: Salesforce Data Model & Object Architecture
children.description: Design efficient and scalable data models using standard and custom objects. Understand different relationship types (Lookup, Master-Detail, Many-to-Many using Junction Objects), external objects, schema builder, field history tracking, and data storage considerations.

children.name: Salesforce Security & Access Control Model
children.description: Implement a multi-layered security model by understanding Organization-Wide Defaults (OWD), Role Hierarchy, Sharing Rules (owner-based, criteria-based), Manual Sharing, Profiles, Permission Sets, Public Groups, Queues, Territory Management, and Field-Level Security (FLS) to control data visibility and access effectively.

tree.name: Salesforce Developer Core Skills
tree.description: Acquire foundational programming and declarative automation skills using Apex, SOQL, Lightning Web Components, and essential developer tools for custom solutions.

resources.title: How to Become a Salesforce Developer in 100 Days (Salesforce Hulk)

children.name: Developer Tools & Development Environments
children.description: Set up Salesforce CLI, VS Code with Salesforce extensions (Apex, LWC, Aura Components, ESLint, Prettier), understand different development environments (Developer Orgs, Sandboxes - Dev, Dev Pro, Partial, Full), Scratch Orgs, and efficient development workflows for a productive and collaborative environment.

children.name: Apex Programming Language Fundamentals
children.description: Learn Apex syntax, data types, variables, operators, control flow statements (if/else, loops), collections (Lists, Sets, Maps), DML operations, database methods, exception handling, classes, objects, interfaces, inheritance, polymorphism, and basic SOQL/SOSL integration within Apex. Understand Apex best practices like bulkification and avoiding hardcoding.

children.name: SOQL & SOSL for Data Manipulation
children.description: Master Salesforce Object Query Language (SOQL) for efficient data retrieval, including relationship queries (parent-to-child, child-to-parent), aggregate functions, and understanding query performance. Utilize Salesforce Object Search Language (SOSL) for full-text searches across multiple objects and fields.

children.name: Apex Triggers, Automation & Best Practices
children.description: Develop bulk-safe and efficient Apex Triggers, understand trigger context variables, trigger order of execution, and implement best practices such as one trigger per object pattern and trigger handler classes. Compare and contrast Apex triggers with Salesforce Flow for automation use cases.

children.name: Asynchronous Apex Techniques
children.description: Implement asynchronous processing using Future Methods, Batch Apex for large data sets, Queueable Apex for more complex chaining, and Scheduled Apex for recurring tasks, understanding their use cases and governor limits.

children.name: Apex Testing, Debugging & Quality Assurance
children.description: Write robust unit tests for Apex classes and triggers, including test data creation (Test.startTest(), Test.stopTest()), mocking callouts, asserting expected results, and achieving the required code coverage. Utilize debug logs, system.debug statements, and the Developer Console for efficient troubleshooting and performance analysis of Apex code.

children.name: Lightning Web Components (LWC) Fundamentals
children.description: Build modern and performant user interfaces using HTML templates, JavaScript controllers, and CSS. Master key LWC concepts such as decorators (@api, @track, @wire), data binding, component composition, lifecycle hooks, event handling (custom events, standard events), and understanding the Lightning Data Service (LDS) for efficient data interaction.

tree.name: Advanced Salesforce Development & Practices
tree.description: Deep dive into advanced development patterns, performance optimization, security best practices, and event-driven architecture within the Salesforce platform.

children.name: Advanced Apex Design Patterns & Frameworks
children.description: Apply advanced architectural patterns for scalable and maintainable Apex development, including Trigger Frameworks (e.g., fflib), Service Layer, Domain Layer, Selector Layer, Unit of Work patterns, and enterprise-grade architecture considerations.

children.name: LWC Advanced Concepts, Performance & Best Practices
children.description: Implement advanced inter-component communication patterns (pub-sub, Lightning Message Service), dynamic component creation, working with third-party JavaScript libraries, performance optimization techniques (memoization, lazy loading), accessibility considerations, and advanced styling in LWCs.

children.name: Governor Limits, Scalability & Performance Optimization
children.description: Gain an in-depth understanding of all Salesforce Governor Limits (CPU time, SOQL queries, DML statements, heap size, etc.). Design and implement solutions to proactively avoid hitting limits, optimize SOQL and DML operations, manage large data volumes, and ensure application scalability and performance.

children.name: Event-Driven Architecture: Platform Events & CDC
children.description: Design and implement event-driven architectures using Platform Events for custom notifications and integrations, and Change Data Capture (CDC) for near real-time data synchronization with external systems. Understand the CometD streaming API for subscribing to these events.

children.name: Secure Development Practices & Code Review
children.description: Implement robust security best practices in Apex (CRUD/FLS enforcement using Schema methods and WITH USER_MODE, SOQL Injection prevention with 'escapeSingleQuotes', CSRF protection) and LWC (XSS prevention, Locker Service compliance, CSP) to build secure and compliant applications. Understand common security vulnerabilities and how to mitigate them.

children.name: Custom Metadata Types & Custom Settings
children.description: Understand and implement Custom Metadata Types and Custom Settings for storing configurable application data, promoting reusability, and reducing hardcoding in Apex and Flow for flexible and easily maintainable solutions.

tree.name: Integrations & DevOps
tree.description: Master techniques for connecting Salesforce with external systems, managing source code effectively, and implementing modern deployment pipelines.

children.name: Salesforce APIs: REST, SOAP, Metadata, Bulk, Streaming
children.description: Master various Salesforce APIs for programmatic access: REST API for general data operations, SOAP API for complex integrations, Metadata API for programmatic metadata deployment and retrieval, Bulk API for large-scale data operations, and Streaming API (including Platform Events and CDC) for real-time notifications. Understand API authentication methods (OAuth, Session ID).

children.name: External Integrations & Apex Callouts
children.description: Integrate Salesforce with external web services using Apex HTTP Callouts, Named Credentials for secure endpoint configuration, External Services (Mulesoft Composer, Salesforce Connect), and handling various authentication mechanisms (OAuth, API Keys) and data formats (JSON, XML).

children.name: Version Control with Git & GitHub
children.description: Learn Git fundamentals for source code management, including common commands (clone, add, commit, push, pull, branch, merge, rebase), resolving merge conflicts, and collaborating effectively on Salesforce development projects using platforms like GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket.

children.name: Salesforce DX & Modern Metadata Deployment
children.description: Understand the Salesforce DX project structure, manifest files (package.xml), scratch orgs for ephemeral development, source tracking, and perform efficient metadata deployments and retrievals using the Salesforce CLI and VS Code. Explore the Salesforce CLI commands for various development tasks.

children.name: CI/CD Pipeline Fundamentals for Salesforce
children.description: Explore Continuous Integration (CI) and Continuous Delivery/Deployment (CD) concepts. Learn about setting up basic CI/CD pipelines for Salesforce using tools like GitHub Actions, GitLab CI/CD, Azure DevOps, Jenkins, or specialized Salesforce DevOps platforms (e.g., Copado, Gearset). Understand automated testing, static code analysis, and deployment automation.

children.name: Managed Packages & AppExchange Strategies
children.description: Understand the concepts of Unmanaged and Managed Packages. Learn how to create, test, and deploy managed packages for distributing applications via AppExchange, including considerations for subscriber orgs, security reviews, and versioning.

tree.name: Project & Career Readiness
tree.description: Apply learned skills to real-world projects, understand solution design principles, and thoroughly prepare for professional certifications and job interviews.

children.name: Portfolio Building & Capstone Projects
children.description: Develop and implement a comprehensive Salesforce application or a series of mini-projects showcasing custom objects, declarative automation, Apex, LWC, integrations, CI/CD setup, and robust testing. Document your architectural choices, development process, and create compelling demos and GitHub repositories to present your capabilities.

children.name: Salesforce Solution Design & Architectural Principles
children.description: Understand Salesforce Well-Architected principles (Trust, Clarity, Simplicity, Sustainability, Resiliency, Agility). Learn about various architectural patterns (e.g., integration patterns, data migration strategies), considerations for large-scale enterprise implementations, governance, and effective documentation for solutions. Explore common design challenges and solutions.

children.name: Certification & Job Interview Preparation
children.description: Thoroughly prepare for the Salesforce Platform Developer I and optionally Platform Developer II certifications. Practice common interview questions, scenario-based problem-solving, live coding challenges, and effectively present your portfolio and experience to potential employers. Understand the Salesforce career path and ecosystem roles.

resources.title: Salesforce Platform Developer I Exam Guide

children.name: Advanced Debugging & Troubleshooting Techniques
children.description: Develop advanced skills in diagnosing and resolving complex issues across Apex, LWC, Flows, declarative automation, and integrations. Utilize advanced debugging tools (VS Code debugger, Apex Debugger, browser developer tools), event monitoring, Health Check, and various systematic troubleshooting methodologies to identify root causes and implement effective solutions.

children.name: Post-Deployment & Application Maintenance
children.description: Understand best practices for post-deployment activities, including monitoring application performance, managing change requests, handling bug fixes, implementing continuous improvement, and documenting ongoing maintenance procedures for Salesforce applications.
